source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב רַגְלָ֑יו וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אַ֥רְצָה בְנֵי־קֶֽדֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And lifted up Jacob his feet and went to [the] land of [the] sons of [the] east.

en.L: And Jacob lifted up his feet and went to the land of the people of the east.
en.B: Jacob went on his way and came to the land of the eastern peoples.
en.R: Jacob continued his trip and came to the land of the people of the east.

es.L: Y alzó Jacob sus pies y fue a la tierra de los hijos del oriente.
es.B: Jacob siguió su camino y llegó a la tierra de los pueblos del oriente.
es.R: Jacob continuó su viaje y llegó a la tierra de la gente del oriente.

fr.L: Et Jacob leva ses pieds et s’en alla au pays des fils de l’Orient.
fr.B: Jacob reprit sa route et arriva au pays des peuples de l’Orient.
fr.R: Jacob a continué son voyage et il est arrivé au pays des gens de l’Est.

sw.L: Yakobo aliinua miguu yake, akaenda katika nchi ya wana wa mashariki.
sw.B: Yakobo aliendelea na safari yake, akafika katika nchi ya mataifa ya mashariki.
sw.R: Yakobo aliendelea kusafiri mpaka akafika kwenye nchi ya watu wa upande wa mashariki.

decisions.choice: lifted up his feet: set off, went on his way
decisions.reason: The expression occurs only here. It may simply mean that Jacob set out, or suggest that he went on with fresh heart after God's promise at Bethel (28:15).

decisions.choice: the people of the east: the peoples beyond the Jordan and the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The people of the east" (benei qedem) is a general name for the tribes east of Canaan (Judges 6:3; Job 1:3). Here it is the region of Haran (verse 4).

decisions.choice: went on his way (B); continued his trip (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m1).

decisions.choice: passé simple for narration at Literal and Balanced ("leva", "reprit"); passé composé at Readable ("a continué")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple at Literal and Balanced, the passé composé, the tense of spoken French, at Readable.

source.text: וַיַּ֞רְא וְהִנֵּ֧ה בְאֵ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֞ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶדְרֵי־צֹאן֙ רֹבְצִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֚י מִן־הַבְּאֵ֣ר הַהִ֔וא יַשְׁק֖וּ הָעֲדָרִ֑ים וְהָאֶ֥בֶן גְּדֹלָ֖ה עַל־פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he looked, and look, a well in the field, and look, there three flocks of sheep [were] lying beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks; and the stone [was] large over [the] mouth of the well.

en.L: And he looked, and look, [there was] a well in the field, and look, three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks. And the stone over the mouth of the well was large.
en.B: There he saw a well out in the open country, with three flocks of sheep lying beside it, because the flocks were watered from that well. A big stone covered the opening of the well.
en.R: He saw a well in a field. Three flocks of sheep were lying near it, because the shepherds got water for their sheep from that well. There was a big stone over the top of the well.

es.L: Y miró, y he aquí, [había] un pozo en el campo, y he aquí, tres rebaños de ovejas estaban echados allí junto a él, porque de aquel pozo abrevaban los rebaños. Y la piedra sobre la boca del pozo era grande.
es.B: Allí vio un pozo en pleno campo, y junto a él estaban echados tres rebaños de ovejas, porque en ese pozo se daba de beber a los rebaños. Una gran piedra tapaba la boca del pozo.
es.R: Vio un pozo en un campo. Cerca de él estaban echados tres rebaños de ovejas, porque los pastores sacaban agua de ese pozo para sus ovejas. Encima del pozo había una piedra grande.

fr.L: Et il regarda, et voici, [il y avait] un puits dans la campagne, et voici, trois troupeaux de moutons étaient couchés là, près de lui, car c’est à ce puits qu’on abreuvait les troupeaux. Et la pierre sur l’ouverture du puits était grande.
fr.B: Là, il vit un puits en pleine campagne, avec trois troupeaux de moutons couchés à côté, car c’est à ce puits qu’on faisait boire les troupeaux. Une grosse pierre fermait l’ouverture du puits.
fr.R: Il a vu un puits dans un champ. Trois troupeaux de moutons étaient couchés près du puits, car les bergers y donnaient à boire à leurs moutons. Il y avait une grosse pierre sur le puits.

sw.L: Naye akatazama, na tazama, [palikuwa na] kisima kondeni, na tazama, makundi matatu ya kondoo yalikuwa yamelala pale kando yake, kwa maana kutoka kisima hicho waliyanywesha makundi. Na jiwe juu ya mdomo wa kisima lilikuwa kubwa.
sw.B: Huko aliona kisima mbugani, na makundi matatu ya kondoo yamelala kando yake, kwa sababu makundi yalinyweshwa maji kutoka kisima hicho. Jiwe kubwa lilifunika mdomo wa kisima.
sw.R: Aliona kisima kondeni. Makundi matatu ya kondoo yalikuwa yamelala karibu nacho, kwa sababu wachungaji waliwanywesha kondoo wao maji ya kisima hicho. Kulikuwa na jiwe kubwa juu ya kisima.

decisions.choice: a well: where wives are found
decisions.reason: Abraham's servant found Rebekah at a well near this same town (24:11-15), and Moses will meet his wife at a well (Exodus 2:15-21). The reader expects a meeting.

decisions.choice: the stone was large: a cover to protect the water
decisions.reason: A heavy stone kept the well clean and kept anyone from drawing water alone. By local custom it was moved only when all the shepherds had gathered (verses 3, 8).

source.text: וְנֶאֶסְפוּ־שָׁ֣מָּה כָל־הָעֲדָרִ֗ים וְגָלֲל֤וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וְהִשְׁק֖וּ אֶת־הַצֹּ֑אן וְהֵשִׁ֧יבוּ אֶת־הָאֶ֛בֶן עַל־פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵ֖ר לִמְקֹמָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they would gather there all the flocks, and they would roll the stone from over [the] mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put back the stone over [the] mouth of the well in its place.

en.L: And all the flocks would be gathered there, and they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place over the mouth of the well.
en.B: The custom was that when all the flocks had gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone off the well's opening and water the sheep, and then put the stone back in place over the opening.
en.R: When all the flocks came together, the shepherds would roll the stone away and give water to the sheep. Then they would put the stone back over the well.

es.L: Y se juntaban allí todos los rebaños, y hacían rodar la piedra de sobre la boca del pozo y abrevaban las ovejas, y volvían a poner la piedra en su lugar sobre la boca del pozo.
es.B: La costumbre era que, cuando se habían reunido allí todos los rebaños, los pastores quitaban rodando la piedra de la boca del pozo y daban de beber a las ovejas, y luego volvían a colocar la piedra en su sitio sobre la boca del pozo.
es.R: Cuando se juntaban todos los rebaños, los pastores hacían rodar la piedra a un lado y daban agua a las ovejas. Después volvían a poner la piedra sobre el pozo.

fr.L: Et tous les troupeaux se rassemblaient là, et on roulait la pierre de dessus l’ouverture du puits, et on abreuvait les moutons, puis on remettait la pierre à sa place sur l’ouverture du puits.
fr.B: C’était la coutume : quand tous les troupeaux s’étaient rassemblés là, les bergers roulaient la pierre pour dégager l’ouverture du puits et faisaient boire les moutons, puis ils remettaient la pierre en place sur l’ouverture.
fr.R: Quand tous les troupeaux étaient réunis, les bergers roulaient la pierre sur le côté et donnaient à boire aux moutons. Ensuite, ils remettaient la pierre sur le puits.

sw.L: Makundi yote yalikuwa yakikusanyika huko, nao walikuwa wakilivingirisha jiwe kutoka juu ya mdomo wa kisima na kuwanywesha kondoo, kisha wakilirudisha jiwe mahali pake juu ya mdomo wa kisima.
sw.B: Desturi ilikuwa hivi: makundi yote yalipokusanyika huko, wachungaji walilivingirisha jiwe kutoka kwenye mdomo wa kisima, wakawanywesha kondoo, kisha wakalirudisha jiwe mahali pake juu ya kisima.
sw.R: Makundi yote yalipokutana, wachungaji hulivingirisha jiwe kando na kuwapa kondoo maji. Kisha hulirudisha jiwe juu ya kisima.

decisions.choice: would gather ... would roll: what was usually done
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe a regular practice, not one event: this is how the well was always used.

decisions.choice: the shepherds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who did the work, as verse 8 makes clear.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב אַחַ֖י מֵאַ֣יִן אַתֶּ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵחָרָ֖ן אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Jacob, my brothers, from where [are] you? And they said, from Haran [are] we.

en.L: And Jacob said to them, "My brothers, where are you from?" And they said, "We are from Haran."
en.B: "Friends, where are you from?" Jacob asked them. "From Haran," they answered.
en.R: Jacob asked the shepherds, "My friends, where do you come from?" They answered, "We are from Haran."

es.L: Y les dijo Jacob: «Hermanos míos, ¿de dónde {{plural_you:son|sois}}?». Y ellos dijeron: «Somos de Harán».
es.B: «Amigos, ¿de dónde {{plural_you:son|sois}}?», les preguntó Jacob. «De Harán», respondieron.
es.R: Jacob les preguntó a los pastores: «Amigos míos, ¿de dónde {{plural_you:vienen|venís}}?». Ellos respondieron: «Somos de Harán».

fr.L: Et Jacob leur dit : « Mes frères, d’où êtes-vous ? » Et ils dirent : « Nous sommes de Harân. »
fr.B: « Mes amis, d’où êtes-vous ? » leur demanda Jacob. « De Harân », répondirent-ils.
fr.R: Jacob a demandé aux bergers : « Mes amis, d’où venez-vous ? » Ils ont répondu : « Nous venons de Harân. »

sw.L: Yakobo akawaambia, "Ndugu zangu, ninyi ni wa wapi?" Wakasema, "Sisi ni wa Harani."
sw.B: "Rafiki zangu, mnatoka wapi?" Yakobo akawauliza. "Tunatoka Harani," wakajibu.
sw.R: Yakobo akawauliza wachungaji, "Rafiki zangu, ninyi mnatoka sehemu gani?" Wakajibu, "Sisi tunatoka Harani."

decisions.choice: my brothers: a friendly greeting to strangers
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is a courteous address, not a claim of kinship.

decisions.choice: Friends (B); My friends (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the friendly greeting (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם הַיְדַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־לָבָ֣ן בֶּן־נָח֑וֹר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יָדָֽעְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, do you know Laban, son of Nahor? And they said, we know [him].

en.L: And he said to them, "Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?" And they said, "We know [him]."
en.B: "Do you know Laban, Nahor's grandson?" he asked. "Yes, we know him," they said.
en.R: Jacob asked them, "Do you know Laban, the grandson of Nahor?" They answered, "Yes, we know him."

es.L: Y les dijo: «¿{{plural_you:Conocen|Conocéis}} a Labán, hijo de Nacor?». Y dijeron: «[Lo] conocemos».
es.B: «¿{{plural_you:Conocen|Conocéis}} a Labán, el nieto de Nacor?», preguntó. «Sí, lo conocemos», dijeron.
es.R: Jacob les preguntó: «¿{{plural_you:Conocen|Conocéis}} a Labán, el nieto de Nacor?». Ellos respondieron: «Sí, lo conocemos».

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « Connaissez-vous Laban, fils de Nahor ? » Et ils dirent : « Nous [le] connaissons. »
fr.B: « Connaissez-vous Laban, le petit-fils de Nahor ? » demanda-t-il. « Oui, nous le connaissons », dirent-ils.
fr.R: Jacob leur a demandé : « Est-ce que vous connaissez Laban, le petit-fils de Nahor ? » Ils ont répondu : « Oui, nous le connaissons. »

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Mnamjua Labani mwana wa Nahori?" Wakasema, "Tunamjua."
sw.B: "Mnamfahamu Labani, mjukuu wa Nahori?" akauliza. "Ndiyo, tunamfahamu," wakasema.
sw.R: Yakobo akawauliza, "Je, mnamjua Labani, mjukuu wa Nahori?" Wakajibu, "Ndiyo, tunamjua."

decisions.choice: the son of Nahor: Nahor's descendant
decisions.reason: Laban was the son of Bethuel and grandson of Nahor, Abraham's brother (24:15, 29). "Son" often means a descendant, and Nahor was the head of the family.

decisions.choice: grandson
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the relationship as it was (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָהֶ֖ם הֲשָׁל֣וֹם ל֑וֹ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ שָׁל֔וֹם וְהִנֵּה֙ רָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ בָּאָ֖ה עִם־הַצֹּֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, [is there] peace to him? And they said, peace; and look, Rachel his daughter [is] coming with the sheep.

en.L: And he said to them, "Is it well with him?" And they said, "[It is] well; and look, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep."
en.B: "Is he well?" he asked. "He is," they replied, "and here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep now."
en.R: Jacob asked, "Is he well?" They said, "Yes, he is. Look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep."

es.L: Y les dijo: «¿Le va bien?». Y dijeron: «[Le va] bien; y he aquí, Raquel su hija viene con las ovejas».
es.B: «¿Está bien de salud?», preguntó. «Sí», respondieron, «y mira, ahí viene ahora su hija Raquel con las ovejas».
es.R: Jacob preguntó: «¿Está bien?». Ellos dijeron: «Sí, está bien. Mira, ahí viene su hija Raquel con las ovejas».

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « Est-il en paix ? » Et ils dirent : « [Il est en] paix ; et voici Rachel, sa fille, qui vient avec les moutons. »
fr.B: « Va-t-il bien ? » demanda-t-il. « Oui, répondirent-ils, et voici justement sa fille Rachel qui arrive avec les moutons. »
fr.R: Jacob a demandé : « Est-ce qu’il va bien ? » Ils ont dit : « Oui, il va bien. Regarde, voici sa fille Rachel qui arrive avec les moutons. »

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Je, ana amani?" Wakasema, "[Ana] amani; na tazama, Raheli binti yake anakuja pamoja na kondoo."
sw.B: "Je, yu mzima?" akauliza. "Yu mzima," wakajibu, "na tazama, binti yake Raheli anakuja sasa na kondoo."
sw.R: Yakobo akauliza, "Je, yeye ni mzima?" Wakasema, "Ndiyo, ni mzima. Tazama, binti yake Raheli anakuja na kondoo."

decisions.choice: is it well with him? (hashalom lo): the usual greeting
decisions.reason: To ask after someone's shalom is to ask about their health and welfare (43:27).

decisions.choice: Rachel: "ewe"
decisions.reason: The name means a female sheep. Rachel first appears as a shepherd with her father's flock (verse 9).

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵ֥ן עוֹד֙ הַיּ֣וֹם גָּד֔וֹל לֹא־עֵ֖ת הֵאָסֵ֣ף הַמִּקְנֶ֑ה הַשְׁק֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן וּלְכ֥וּ רְעֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, look, still the day [is] great; not [is it the] time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and go, pasture [them].

en.L: And he said, "Look, it is still high day; it is not time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep and go, pasture [them]."
en.B: "But it is the middle of the day," Jacob said, "far too early to bring the animals in. Why not water the sheep and take them back to graze?"
en.R: Jacob said, "It is still the middle of the day. It is not time yet to bring the animals in for the night. Give the sheep some water. Then take them back out to eat grass."

es.L: Y dijo: «He aquí, todavía es pleno día; no es hora de recoger el ganado. {{plural_you:Abreven|Abrevad}} las ovejas {{plural_you:y vayan|e id}} a apacentar[las]».
es.B: «Pero todavía es pleno día», dijo Jacob, «demasiado temprano para recoger los animales. ¿Por qué no {{plural_you:dan|dais}} de beber a las ovejas y {{plural_you:las llevan|las lleváis}} otra vez a pastar?».
es.R: Jacob dijo: «Todavía es mediodía. No es hora de encerrar a los animales para la noche. {{plural_you:Denles|Dadles}} agua a las ovejas. Después {{plural_you:llévenlas|llevadlas}} otra vez a comer pasto».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Voici, le jour est encore haut ; ce n’est pas le moment de rassembler le bétail. Abreuvez les moutons, et allez, faites[-les] paître. »
fr.B: « Mais il fait encore grand jour, dit Jacob, il est bien trop tôt pour rentrer les bêtes. Pourquoi ne pas faire boire les moutons et les ramener au pâturage ? »
fr.R: Jacob a dit : « On est encore au milieu de la journée. Ce n’est pas encore l’heure de rentrer les bêtes pour la nuit. Donnez de l’eau aux moutons. Puis emmenez-les de nouveau brouter l’herbe. »

sw.L: Akasema, "Tazama, bado ni mchana mkuu; si wakati wa kukusanya mifugo. Wanywesheni kondoo, mwende mkawachunge."
sw.B: "Lakini bado ni adhuhuri," Yakobo akasema, "ni mapema mno kuwarudisha wanyama. Kwa nini msiwanyweshe kondoo na kuwarudisha malishoni?"
sw.R: Yakobo akasema, "Bado ni mchana. Si wakati wa kuwaingiza wanyama zizini kwa ajili ya usiku. Wapeni kondoo maji. Kisha warudisheni wakale majani."

decisions.choice: the day is still great: it is broad daylight
decisions.reason: Much of the day is left. Jacob, a skilled herdsman, sees no reason for the flocks to wait idle; he may also want the shepherds gone before Rachel arrives.

decisions.choice: Why not water the sheep ...?
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the stranger's command as a suggestion, which is how it would be heard.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:y vayan|e id}}
alternatives: {{plural_you:vayan|id}} with the conjunction outside the span
decisions.reason: Before "id" Spanish writes "e" instead of "y", so the conjunction goes inside the plural-you span for both forms to read correctly.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לֹ֣א נוּכַל֒ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֲדָרִ֔ים וְגָֽלֲלוּ֙ אֶת־הָאֶ֔בֶן מֵעַ֖ל פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֑ר וְהִשְׁקִ֖ינוּ הַצֹּֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, not we are able, until are gathered all the flocks and they roll the stone from over [the] mouth of the well; then we water the sheep.

en.L: And they said, "We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep."
en.B: "We are not allowed to," they answered, "until all the flocks have come in and the stone has been rolled off the well. Then we can water the sheep."
en.R: They answered, "We cannot do that until all the flocks are here. Then the stone is rolled away, and we give water to the sheep."

es.L: Y dijeron: «No podemos, hasta que se junten todos los rebaños y hagan rodar la piedra de la boca del pozo; entonces abrevamos las ovejas».
es.B: «No nos está permitido», respondieron, «hasta que hayan llegado todos los rebaños y se haya quitado la piedra del pozo. Entonces podemos dar de beber a las ovejas».
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «No podemos hacerlo hasta que estén aquí todos los rebaños. Entonces se quita la piedra y les damos agua a las ovejas».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Nous ne pouvons pas, jusqu’à ce que tous les troupeaux soient rassemblés et qu’on roule la pierre de dessus l’ouverture du puits ; alors nous abreuvons les moutons. »
fr.B: « Nous n’en avons pas le droit, répondirent-ils, tant que tous les troupeaux ne sont pas arrivés et que la pierre n’a pas été roulée hors du puits. Alors nous pouvons faire boire les moutons. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Nous ne pouvons pas le faire avant que tous les troupeaux soient là. Ensuite, on roule la pierre et nous donnons à boire aux moutons. »

sw.L: Wakasema, "Hatuwezi, mpaka makundi yote yakusanywe na walivingirishe jiwe kutoka juu ya mdomo wa kisima; ndipo tuwanyweshe kondoo."
sw.B: "Hatuna ruhusa," wakajibu, "mpaka makundi yote yafike na jiwe liondolewe kisimani. Ndipo tunaweza kuwanywesha kondoo."
sw.R: Wakajibu, "Hatuwezi kufanya hivyo mpaka makundi yote yawe hapa. Kisha jiwe huondolewa, nasi tunawapa kondoo maji."

decisions.choice: we cannot: it is not done, or not possible
decisions.reason: The shepherds may mean that custom forbids it, or that the stone is too heavy for a few of them. Jacob then moves it alone (verse 10).

source.text: עוֹדֶ֖נּוּ מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֑ם וְרָחֵ֣ל׀בָּ֗אָה עִם־הַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יהָ כִּ֥י רֹעָ֖ה הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: Still he [was] speaking with them, and Rachel came with the sheep that [belonged] to her father, for a shepherdess [was] she.

en.L: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
en.B: He was still talking with them when Rachel arrived with her father's sheep, since she was the one who looked after them.
en.R: While Jacob was still talking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep. She took care of them.

es.L: Todavía estaba él hablando con ellos, cuando Raquel llegó con las ovejas de su padre, porque ella era pastora.
es.B: Aún estaba hablando con ellos cuando llegó Raquel con las ovejas de su padre, pues era ella quien las cuidaba.
es.R: Mientras Jacob todavía hablaba con ellos, llegó Raquel con las ovejas de su padre. Ella las cuidaba.

fr.L: Il parlait encore avec eux, et Rachel vint avec les moutons de son père, car elle était bergère.
fr.B: Il parlait encore avec eux quand Rachel arriva avec les moutons de son père, car c’était elle qui les gardait.
fr.R: Jacob parlait encore avec eux quand Rachel est arrivée avec les moutons de son père. C’était elle qui s’occupait d’eux.

sw.L: Alipokuwa bado akizungumza nao, Raheli akaja pamoja na kondoo wa baba yake, kwa maana yeye alikuwa mchungaji.
sw.B: Alikuwa bado anaongea nao Raheli alipofika na kondoo wa baba yake, kwa kuwa yeye ndiye aliyekuwa akiwachunga.
sw.R: Yakobo alipokuwa bado anaongea nao, Raheli alifika na kondoo wa baba yake. Yeye ndiye aliyewatunza.

decisions.choice: a shepherdess: a daughter tending the family flock
decisions.reason: Daughters often helped with the flocks (Exodus 2:16). The word is the feminine of the ordinary word for shepherd.

source.text: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ רָאָ֨ה יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת־רָחֵ֗ל בַּת־לָבָן֙ אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֔וֹ וְאֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיָּ֤גֶל אֶת־הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיַּ֕שְׁקְ אֶת־צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when saw Jacob Rachel, daughter of Laban, brother of his mother, and [the] sheep of Laban, brother of his mother, and drew near Jacob and rolled the stone from over [the] mouth of the well and watered [the] sheep of Laban, brother of his mother.

en.L: And when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, Jacob went up and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well and watered the sheep of Laban his mother's brother.
en.B: When Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his uncle Laban, with Laban's sheep, he stepped forward, rolled the stone off the well's opening by himself, and watered his uncle's flock.
en.R: Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother's brother Laban, with Laban's sheep. He went to the well and rolled the stone away by himself. Then he gave water to Laban's sheep.

es.L: Y cuando vio Jacob a Raquel, hija de Labán, hermano de su madre, y las ovejas de Labán, hermano de su madre, se acercó Jacob e hizo rodar la piedra de la boca del pozo y abrevó las ovejas de Labán, hermano de su madre.
es.B: Cuando Jacob vio a Raquel, la hija de su tío Labán, con las ovejas de Labán, se adelantó, quitó él solo la piedra de la boca del pozo y dio de beber al rebaño de su tío.
es.R: Jacob vio a Raquel, la hija de Labán, el hermano de su madre, con las ovejas de Labán. Fue al pozo y quitó la piedra él solo. Después les dio agua a las ovejas de Labán.

fr.L: Et lorsque Jacob vit Rachel, fille de Laban, frère de sa mère, et les moutons de Laban, frère de sa mère, Jacob s’approcha et roula la pierre de dessus l’ouverture du puits, et il abreuva les moutons de Laban, frère de sa mère.
fr.B: Dès que Jacob vit Rachel, la fille de son oncle Laban, avec les moutons de Laban, il s’avança, roula à lui seul la pierre qui fermait le puits et fit boire le troupeau de son oncle.
fr.R: Jacob a vu Rachel, la fille de Laban, le frère de sa mère, avec les moutons de Laban. Il est allé au puits et il a roulé la pierre tout seul. Puis il a donné à boire aux moutons de Laban.

sw.L: Ikawa Yakobo alipomwona Raheli binti Labani, ndugu wa mama yake, na kondoo wa Labani, ndugu wa mama yake, Yakobo akakaribia, akalivingirisha jiwe kutoka juu ya mdomo wa kisima, akawanywesha kondoo wa Labani, ndugu wa mama yake.
sw.B: Yakobo alipomwona Raheli, binti wa mjomba wake Labani, pamoja na kondoo wa Labani, alisogea mbele, akalivingirisha peke yake jiwe kutoka mdomo wa kisima, akalinywesha kundi la mjomba wake.
sw.R: Yakobo alimwona Raheli, binti wa Labani kaka wa mama yake, akiwa na kondoo wa Labani. Akaenda kisimani, akalivingirisha jiwe peke yake. Kisha akawapa maji kondoo wa Labani.

decisions.choice: his mother's brother: three times in one verse
decisions.reason: The repetition shows what fills Jacob's mind: these are his mother's people, the family he was sent to (28:2).

decisions.choice: rolled the stone: alone, against custom
decisions.reason: Jacob does by himself what the shepherds said needed all of them (verse 8). It shows his strength and his eagerness, and it serves Rachel as Rebekah once served Abraham's servant at a well (24:18-20).

decisions.choice: by himself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out what the context shows (verses 3, 8).

source.text: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק יַעֲקֹ֖ב לְרָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And kissed Jacob Rachel, and he lifted up his voice and wept.

en.L: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice and wept.
en.B: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and broke into loud weeping.
en.R: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and began to cry out loud.

es.L: Y besó Jacob a Raquel, y alzó su voz y lloró.
es.B: Luego Jacob besó a Raquel y rompió en fuerte llanto.
es.R: Entonces Jacob besó a Raquel y se puso a llorar en voz alta.

fr.L: Et Jacob embrassa Rachel, et il éleva la voix et pleura.
fr.B: Puis Jacob embrassa Rachel et éclata en sanglots.
fr.R: Ensuite Jacob a embrassé Rachel et il s’est mis à pleurer très fort.

sw.L: Kisha Yakobo akambusu Raheli, akaipaza sauti yake na kulia.
sw.B: Kisha Yakobo akambusu Raheli, akaangua kilio kikubwa.
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo akambusu Raheli, akaanza kulia kwa sauti.

decisions.choice: kissed: a greeting between relatives
decisions.reason: A kiss was the normal greeting within a family (verse 13; 33:4). Jacob greets his cousin before telling her who he is (verse 12).

decisions.choice: lifted up his voice and wept: wept aloud
decisions.reason: After a long and lonely journey Jacob has reached his mother's family. He weeps from relief and joy.

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֨ד יַעֲקֹ֜ב לְרָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י אֲחִ֤י אָבִ֨יהָ֙ ה֔וּא וְכִ֥י בֶן־רִבְקָ֖ה ה֑וּא וַתָּ֖רָץ וַתַּגֵּ֥ד לְאָבִֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And told Jacob to Rachel that [the] relative of her father [was] he, and that [the] son of Rebekah [was] he. And she ran and told her father.

en.L: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's relative, and that he was Rebekah's son; and she ran and told her father.
en.B: He explained to Rachel that he was a relative of her father, Rebekah's son, and she ran off to tell her father.
en.R: Jacob told Rachel that he was part of her father's family. He was Rebekah's son. Rachel ran and told her father.

es.L: Y Jacob le contó a Raquel que él era pariente de su padre, y que era hijo de Rebeca; y ella corrió y se lo contó a su padre.
es.B: Le explicó a Raquel que era pariente de su padre, hijo de Rebeca, y ella se fue corriendo a decírselo a su padre.
es.R: Jacob le dijo a Raquel que él era de la familia de su padre. Era hijo de Rebeca. Raquel corrió a contárselo a su padre.

fr.L: Et Jacob fit savoir à Rachel qu’il était un parent de son père, et qu’il était le fils de Rébecca ; et elle courut le dire à son père.
fr.B: Il expliqua à Rachel qu’il était un parent de son père, le fils de Rébecca, et elle partit en courant prévenir son père.
fr.R: Jacob a dit à Rachel qu’il faisait partie de la famille de son père. Il était le fils de Rébecca. Rachel a couru le dire à son père.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akamwambia Raheli kwamba yeye ni jamaa wa baba yake, na kwamba yeye ni mwana wa Rebeka; naye akakimbia akamwambia baba yake.
sw.B: Akamweleza Raheli kwamba yeye ni jamaa wa baba yake, mwana wa Rebeka, naye Raheli akakimbia kwenda kumwambia baba yake.
sw.R: Yakobo akamwambia Raheli kwamba yeye ni wa ukoo wa baba yake. Alikuwa mwana wa Rebeka. Raheli akakimbia, akamwambia baba yake.

decisions.choice: her father's relative: literally "her father's brother"
decisions.reason: "Brother" (ach) is used for any close kinsman, as Abraham called Lot his brother (13:8; 14:14). Jacob was Laban's nephew.

decisions.choice: relative
decisions.reason: The general sense of the word is given (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ לָבָ֜ן אֶת־שֵׁ֣מַע׀יַעֲקֹ֣ב בֶּן־אֲחֹת֗וֹ וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיְחַבֶּק־לוֹ֙ וַיְנַשֶּׁק־ל֔וֹ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר לְלָבָ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard Laban [the] report of Jacob, son of his sister, and he ran to meet him and embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house; and he recounted to Laban all these things.

en.L: And when Laban heard the news of Jacob his sister's son, he ran to meet him and embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.
en.B: As soon as Laban heard about Jacob, his sister's son, he ran out to meet him, hugged and kissed him, and took him home. Jacob told Laban everything that had happened.
en.R: When Laban heard that his sister's son Jacob was there, he ran out to meet him. He hugged him and kissed him and brought him to his home. Jacob told Laban all about what had happened.

es.L: Y cuando oyó Labán la noticia de Jacob, hijo de su hermana, corrió a su encuentro y lo abrazó y lo besó y lo llevó a su casa. Y él le contó a Labán todas estas cosas.
es.B: En cuanto Labán oyó hablar de Jacob, el hijo de su hermana, salió corriendo a recibirlo, lo abrazó, lo besó y se lo llevó a su casa. Jacob le contó a Labán todo lo que había pasado.
es.R: Cuando Labán supo que Jacob, el hijo de su hermana, estaba allí, salió corriendo a recibirlo. Lo abrazó, lo besó y lo llevó a su casa. Jacob le contó a Labán todo lo que había sucedido.

fr.L: Et quand Laban entendit la nouvelle de Jacob, fils de sa sœur, il courut à sa rencontre, l’étreignit, l’embrassa et l’amena dans sa maison. Et il raconta à Laban toutes ces choses.
fr.B: Dès que Laban entendit parler de Jacob, le fils de sa sœur, il courut au-devant de lui, le serra dans ses bras, l’embrassa et l’emmena chez lui. Jacob raconta à Laban tout ce qui s’était passé.
fr.R: Quand Laban a appris que Jacob, le fils de sa sœur, était là, il a couru à sa rencontre. Il l’a serré dans ses bras, il l’a embrassé et il l’a emmené chez lui. Jacob a raconté à Laban tout ce qui lui était arrivé.

sw.L: Ikawa Labani aliposikia habari za Yakobo, mwana wa dada yake, akakimbia kumlaki, akamkumbatia, akambusu, akamleta nyumbani kwake. Naye akamweleza Labani mambo hayo yote.
sw.B: Mara Labani aliposikia habari za Yakobo, mwana wa dada yake, alitoka mbio kwenda kumlaki, akamkumbatia na kumbusu, akampeleka nyumbani. Yakobo akamsimulia Labani yote yaliyotokea.
sw.R: Labani aliposikia kwamba Yakobo, mwana wa dada yake, amefika, alikimbia kwenda kumlaki. Akamkumbatia, akambusu, akampeleka nyumbani kwake. Yakobo akamweleza Labani habari zote za yaliyompata.

decisions.choice: he ran ... embraced ... kissed ... brought him to his house: Laban's warm welcome
decisions.reason: Laban had run out to meet Abraham's servant once he saw the gold given to Rebekah (24:29-31). Jacob comes with no camels or gifts; how Laban treats him will soon be seen.

decisions.choice: all these things: Jacob's story
decisions.reason: What Jacob told is not said: probably his journey and why he came, perhaps also what happened with Esau.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לָבָ֔ן אַ֛ךְ עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עִמּ֖וֹ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him Laban, surely my bone and my flesh [are] you. And he stayed with him a month of days.

en.L: And Laban said to him, "Surely you are my bone and my flesh!" And he stayed with him a full month.
en.B: "You really are my own bone and flesh!" Laban said to him. Jacob stayed on with him for a whole month.
en.R: Laban said to him, "You really are part of my own family!" Jacob stayed with Laban for a month.

es.L: Y le dijo Labán: «¡Ciertamente tú eres mi hueso y mi carne!». Y se quedó con él un mes entero.
es.B: «¡De veras eres mi propio hueso y mi propia carne!», le dijo Labán. Jacob se quedó con él todo un mes.
es.R: Labán le dijo: «¡De verdad eres de mi propia familia!». Jacob se quedó con Labán un mes.

fr.L: Et Laban lui dit : « Assurément, tu es mon os et ma chair ! » Et il demeura chez lui un mois entier.
fr.B: « Tu es vraiment de mes os et de ma chair ! » lui dit Laban. Jacob resta chez lui tout un mois.
fr.R: Laban lui a dit : « Tu fais vraiment partie de ma famille ! » Jacob est resté un mois chez Laban.

sw.L: Labani akamwambia, "Kweli wewe ni mfupa wangu na mwili wangu!" Naye akakaa pamoja naye kwa muda wa mwezi mmoja kamili.
sw.B: "Wewe kwa kweli ni mfupa wangu na mwili wangu mwenyewe!" Labani akamwambia. Yakobo akakaa naye mwezi mzima.
sw.R: Labani akamwambia, "Kweli wewe ni mtu wa jamaa yangu mwenyewe!" Yakobo akakaa na Labani kwa mwezi mmoja.

decisions.choice: my bone and my flesh: my own family
decisions.reason: The phrase means close kin (Judges 9:2; 2 Samuel 5:1). It echoes the man's words about the woman in 2:23.

decisions.choice: a month of days: a full month
decisions.reason: The phrase means a whole month, a period of hospitality after which questions of work and wages arise (verse 15).

decisions.choice: part of my own family
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the expression (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב הֲכִי־אָחִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וַעֲבַדְתַּ֖נִי חִנָּ֑ם הַגִּ֥ידָה לִּ֖י מַה־מַּשְׂכֻּרְתֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Laban to Jacob, is it because my relative [are] you that you should serve me for nothing? Tell me, what [will be] your wages?

en.L: And Laban said to Jacob, "Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?"
en.B: Then Laban said to Jacob, "You are my relative, but that is no reason for you to work for me without pay. Tell me what you want to be paid."
en.R: Then Laban said to Jacob, "You are my relative, but you should not have to work for me for nothing. Tell me what I should pay you."

es.L: Y dijo Labán a Jacob: «¿Acaso porque eres mi pariente me vas a servir de balde? Dime, ¿cuál será tu salario?».
es.B: Entonces Labán le dijo a Jacob: «Eres mi pariente, pero eso no es razón para que trabajes para mí sin paga. Dime cuánto quieres ganar».
es.R: Después Labán le dijo a Jacob: «Eres mi pariente, pero no tienes por qué trabajar para mí sin recibir nada. Dime cuánto debo pagarte».

fr.L: Et Laban dit à Jacob : « Parce que tu es mon parent, vas-tu donc me servir pour rien ? Dis-moi quel sera ton salaire. »
fr.B: Puis Laban dit à Jacob : « Tu es mon parent, mais ce n’est pas une raison pour travailler pour moi sans être payé. Dis-moi ce que tu veux comme salaire. »
fr.R: Ensuite Laban a dit à Jacob : « Tu es de ma famille, mais tu ne dois pas travailler pour moi pour rien. Dis-moi combien je dois te payer. »

sw.L: Naye Labani akamwambia Yakobo, "Je, kwa sababu wewe ni jamaa yangu, ndiyo unitumikie bure? Niambie, ujira wako utakuwa nini?"
sw.B: Kisha Labani akamwambia Yakobo, "Wewe ni jamaa yangu, lakini hiyo si sababu ya kunifanyia kazi bila malipo. Niambie unataka kulipwa nini."
sw.R: Kisha Labani akamwambia Yakobo, "Wewe ni ndugu yangu, lakini hupaswi kunifanyia kazi bure. Niambie nikulipe kiasi gani."

decisions.choice: serve me for nothing: the start of a long bargain
decisions.reason: Laban speaks generously, but it makes Jacob a hired worker. The word "wages" returns when Jacob complains that Laban changed his wages ten times (31:7, 41).

decisions.choice: my relative: literally "my brother"
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "brother" means a kinsman.

source.text: וּלְלָבָ֖ן שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֑וֹת שֵׁ֤ם הַגְּדֹלָה֙ לֵאָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַקְּטַנָּ֖ה רָחֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And to Laban [were] two daughters; [the] name of the older [was] Leah, and [the] name of the younger [was] Rachel.

en.L: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
en.B: Laban had two daughters. The elder was called Leah, and the younger Rachel.
en.R: Laban had two daughters. The older one was named Leah, and the younger one was named Rachel.

es.L: Y Labán tenía dos hijas; el nombre de la mayor era Lea, y el nombre de la menor, Raquel.
es.B: Labán tenía dos hijas. La mayor se llamaba Lea, y la menor, Raquel.
es.R: Labán tenía dos hijas. La hija mayor se llamaba Lea, y la hija menor se llamaba Raquel.

fr.L: Or Laban avait deux filles ; le nom de l’aînée était Léa, et le nom de la cadette, Rachel.
fr.B: Laban avait deux filles. L’aînée s’appelait Léa, et la cadette Rachel.
fr.R: Laban avait deux filles. La fille aînée s’appelait Léa, et la plus jeune s’appelait Rachel.

sw.L: Basi Labani alikuwa na binti wawili; jina la mkubwa lilikuwa Lea, na jina la mdogo lilikuwa Raheli.
sw.B: Labani alikuwa na binti wawili. Mkubwa aliitwa Lea, na mdogo Raheli.
sw.R: Labani alikuwa na binti wawili. Binti mkubwa aliitwa Lea, na binti mdogo aliitwa Raheli.

decisions.choice: the older ... the younger: the same words as for Esau and Jacob
decisions.reason: The words are "the big one" and "the small one", as used of Esau and Jacob (27:1, 15). Jacob, the younger who took the older's place, will meet the same question in reverse (verse 26).

decisions.choice: Leah: perhaps "cow"
decisions.reason: The name may mean "wild cow" or come from a word for weariness. Like Rachel ("ewe"), it may be a name from herding life.

source.text: וְעֵינֵ֥י לֵאָ֖ה רַכּ֑וֹת וְרָחֵל֙ הָֽיְתָ֔ה יְפַת־תֹּ֖אַר וִיפַ֥ת מַרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] eyes of Leah [were] weak, but Rachel was beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance.

en.L: And Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and beautiful in appearance.
en.B: Leah's eyes were delicate, but Rachel was shapely and lovely to look at.
en.R: Leah had gentle eyes, but Rachel was very beautiful in both face and body.

es.L: Y los ojos de Lea eran débiles, pero Raquel era hermosa de figura y hermosa de aspecto.
es.B: Lea tenía los ojos delicados, pero Raquel tenía buena figura y era muy bella.
es.R: Lea tenía ojos dulces, pero Raquel era muy hermosa de cara y de cuerpo.

fr.L: Et les yeux de Léa étaient faibles, mais Rachel était belle de taille et belle de visage.
fr.B: Léa avait les yeux délicats, mais Rachel était bien faite et belle à regarder.
fr.R: Léa avait des yeux doux, mais Rachel était très belle, de visage et de corps.

sw.L: Na macho ya Lea yalikuwa dhaifu, lakini Raheli alikuwa mzuri wa umbo na mzuri wa sura.
sw.B: Macho ya Lea yalikuwa laini, lakini Raheli alikuwa na umbo zuri na sura ya kupendeza.
sw.R: Lea alikuwa na macho ya upole, lakini Raheli alikuwa mrembo sana, kwa uso na kwa umbo.

decisions.choice: Leah's eyes were weak (rakkot): soft, tender, or dull
decisions.reason: The word (rakh) means soft or tender. It may be praise (gentle, lovely eyes) or point to eyes without sparkle. The contrast with Rachel suggests Leah's looks were plain beside her sister's.

decisions.choice: beautiful in form and appearance: beautiful in figure and face
decisions.reason: The same pair of words is later used of Joseph, Rachel's son (39:6).

decisions.choice: delicate (B); gentle (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable choose words that keep the uncertainty of the Hebrew (m1).

source.text: וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת־רָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶֽעֱבָדְךָ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים בְּרָחֵ֥ל בִּתְּךָ֖ הַקְּטַנָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And loved Jacob Rachel, and he said, I will serve you seven years for Rachel your daughter, the younger.

en.L: And Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, "I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter."
en.B: Jacob had fallen in love with Rachel, so he said, "I will work for you seven years in return for your younger daughter Rachel."
en.R: Jacob was in love with Rachel. So he said to Laban, "I will work for you for seven years if you will let me marry your younger daughter Rachel."

es.L: Y Jacob amaba a Raquel, y dijo: «Te serviré siete años a cambio de Raquel, tu hija la menor».
es.B: Jacob se había enamorado de Raquel, así que dijo: «Trabajaré para ti siete años a cambio de tu hija menor, Raquel».
es.R: Jacob estaba enamorado de Raquel. Así que le dijo a Labán: «Trabajaré para ti siete años si me dejas casarme con tu hija menor, Raquel».

fr.L: Et Jacob aima Rachel, et il dit : « Je te servirai sept années en échange de Rachel, ta fille, la plus jeune. »
fr.B: Jacob était tombé amoureux de Rachel ; il dit donc : « Je travaillerai sept ans pour toi en échange de ta fille cadette, Rachel. »
fr.R: Jacob était amoureux de Rachel. Alors il a dit à Laban : « Je vais travailler pour toi pendant sept ans si tu me laisses épouser ta fille cadette, Rachel. »

sw.L: Yakobo alimpenda Raheli, akasema, "Nitakutumikia miaka saba kwa malipo ya Raheli, binti yako mdogo."
sw.B: Yakobo alikuwa amempenda Raheli, kwa hiyo akasema, "Nitakufanyia kazi miaka saba ili unipe binti yako mdogo, Raheli."
sw.R: Yakobo alimpenda sana Raheli. Kwa hiyo akamwambia Labani, "Nitakufanyia kazi kwa miaka saba ukiniruhusu nimwoe binti yako mdogo, Raheli."

decisions.choice: seven years for Rachel: work in place of a bride-price
decisions.reason: A bridegroom normally paid the bride's family a price or gifts (24:53; 34:12). Jacob arrived with nothing, so he offers his labor instead. Seven years' work was a very high price.

decisions.choice: your younger daughter: Jacob makes it plain
decisions.reason: Jacob names her and calls her the younger, as if to leave no room for a mistake. Laban will find one anyway (verse 26).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֗ן ט֚וֹבתִּתִּ֣י אֹתָ֣הּ לָ֔ךְ מִתִּתִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ לְאִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֑ר שְׁבָ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Laban, better [is] my giving her to you than my giving her to another man; stay with me.

en.L: And Laban said, "It is better that I give her to you than that I give her to another man; stay with me."
en.B: "Better that she should go to you than to some other man," Laban answered. "Stay here with me."
en.R: Laban said, "It is better for me to give her to you than to someone else. Stay here with me."

es.L: Y dijo Labán: «Mejor es que te la dé a ti que dársela a otro hombre; quédate conmigo».
es.B: «Mejor que sea para ti y no para otro hombre», respondió Labán. «Quédate aquí conmigo».
es.R: Labán dijo: «Es mejor dártela a ti que a otro. Quédate aquí conmigo».

fr.L: Et Laban dit : « Il vaut mieux que je te la donne à toi que de la donner à un autre homme ; reste avec moi. »
fr.B: « Mieux vaut qu’elle soit à toi plutôt qu’à un autre, répondit Laban. Reste ici avec moi. »
fr.R: Laban a dit : « C’est mieux de te la donner à toi qu’à quelqu’un d’autre. Reste ici avec moi. »

sw.L: Labani akasema, "Ni heri mimi kukupa wewe kuliko kumpa mwanamume mwingine; kaa pamoja nami."
sw.B: "Ni bora aolewe nawe kuliko mwanamume mwingine," Labani akajibu. "Kaa hapa pamoja nami."
sw.R: Labani akasema, "Ni vizuri zaidi nimpe wewe kuliko mtu mwingine. Kaa hapa nami."

decisions.choice: it is better that I give her to you: an answer that promises less than it seems
decisions.reason: Laban never says "I will give you Rachel". His careful words leave room for what he does in verse 23.

decisions.choice: than to another man: marriage within the family preferred
decisions.reason: It was thought better for a daughter to marry a kinsman than an outsider (24:3-4; 28:2).

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ד יַעֲקֹ֛ב בְּרָחֵ֖ל שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וַיִּהְי֤וּ בְעֵינָיו֙ כְּיָמִ֣ים אֲחָדִ֔ים בְּאַהֲבָת֖וֹ אֹתָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And served Jacob for Rachel seven years, and they were in his eyes like a few days because of his love for her.

en.L: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they were in his eyes like a few days, because of his love for her.
en.B: So Jacob worked seven years to win Rachel, and because he loved her so much, the years went by for him as if they were only a few days.
en.R: So Jacob worked seven years so he could marry Rachel. He loved her so much that the seven years felt like only a few days.

es.L: Y sirvió Jacob por Raquel siete años, y fueron a sus ojos como unos pocos días, por el amor que le tenía.
es.B: Así que Jacob trabajó siete años para ganarse a Raquel, y como la amaba tanto, los años se le pasaron como si fueran solo unos días.
es.R: Así que Jacob trabajó siete años para poder casarse con Raquel. La amaba tanto que esos siete años le parecieron solo unos pocos días.

fr.L: Et Jacob servit sept ans pour Rachel, et ils furent à ses yeux comme quelques jours, à cause de son amour pour elle.
fr.B: Jacob travailla donc sept ans pour obtenir Rachel, et, tant il l’aimait, ces années passèrent pour lui comme s’il ne s’agissait que de quelques jours.
fr.R: Alors Jacob a travaillé sept ans pour pouvoir épouser Rachel. Il l’aimait tellement que ces sept ans lui ont semblé durer quelques jours seulement.

sw.L: Hivyo Yakobo alitumika kwa malipo ya Raheli miaka saba, na machoni pake ilionekana kama siku chache, kwa sababu ya kumpenda kwake.
sw.B: Basi Yakobo alifanya kazi miaka saba ili ampate Raheli, na kwa sababu alimpenda sana, miaka hiyo ilimpita kana kwamba ni siku chache tu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yakobo alifanya kazi miaka saba ili aweze kumwoa Raheli. Alimpenda sana hata miaka hiyo saba ikaonekana kwake kama siku chache tu.

decisions.choice: a few days: the words Rebekah had used
decisions.reason: Rebekah told Jacob to stay with Laban "a few days" (27:44). The days became years, but love made them seem short.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב אֶל־לָבָן֙ הָבָ֣ה אֶת־אִשְׁתִּ֔י כִּ֥י מָלְא֖וּ יָמָ֑י וְאָב֖וֹאָה אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jacob to Laban, give my wife, for are fulfilled my days, that I may go in to her.

en.L: And Jacob said to Laban, "Give [me] my wife, for my days are completed, that I may go in to her."
en.B: Then Jacob said to Laban, "My time is up. Give me my wife, so that I may sleep with her."
en.R: Then Jacob said to Laban, "I have worked the seven years we agreed on. Now give me Rachel to be my wife so I can live with her as her husband."

es.L: Y dijo Jacob a Labán: «Da[me] mi mujer, porque se han cumplido mis días, para que me llegue a ella».
es.B: Entonces Jacob le dijo a Labán: «Ya se cumplió mi tiempo. Dame a mi esposa, para que me acueste con ella».
es.R: Después Jacob le dijo a Labán: «Ya trabajé los siete años que acordamos. Ahora dame a Raquel por esposa, para que pueda vivir con ella como su marido».

fr.L: Et Jacob dit à Laban : « Donne[-moi] ma femme, car mes jours sont accomplis, et que j’aille vers elle. »
fr.B: Puis Jacob dit à Laban : « Mon temps est terminé. Donne-moi ma femme, pour que je m’unisse à elle. »
fr.R: Ensuite Jacob a dit à Laban : « J’ai travaillé les sept ans dont nous avions convenu. Maintenant, donne-moi Rachel pour femme, pour que je puisse vivre avec elle comme son mari. »

sw.L: Yakobo akamwambia Labani, "Nikabidhi mke wangu, kwa sababu siku zangu zimekamilika, ili niingie kwake."
sw.B: Kisha Yakobo akamwambia Labani, "Muda wangu umekwisha. Nipe mke wangu ili nilale naye."
sw.R: Kisha Yakobo akamwambia Labani, "Nimefanya kazi ile miaka saba tuliyokubaliana. Sasa nipe Raheli awe mke wangu, ili niishi naye kama mume wake."

decisions.choice: my days are completed: my time of service is over
decisions.reason: The agreed seven years are finished (verse 18).

decisions.choice: my wife: Rachel was already pledged to him
decisions.reason: Once a marriage was agreed, the woman could be called the man's wife before the wedding (Deuteronomy 22:23-24).

decisions.choice: go in to her: consummate the marriage
decisions.reason: To "go in to" a woman is a plain way of speaking of sexual union (16:2; 30:3).

decisions.choice: Rachel
decisions.reason: Readable names the wife Jacob means, which matters for verse 25.

source.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף לָבָ֛ן אֶת־כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And gathered Laban all [the] men of the place and made a feast.

en.L: And Laban gathered together all the {{gender:people|men}} of the place and made a feast.
en.B: So Laban invited all the {{gender:people|men}} of the place and gave a wedding feast.
en.R: So Laban invited all the {{gender:people|men}} who lived there to a wedding feast.

es.L: Y reunió Labán a {{gender:toda la gente|todos los hombres}} del lugar e hizo un banquete.
es.B: Así que Labán invitó a {{gender:toda la gente|todos los hombres}} del lugar y ofreció un banquete de bodas.
es.R: Entonces Labán invitó a una fiesta de bodas a {{gender:toda la gente que vivía|todos los hombres que vivían}} allí.

fr.L: Et Laban rassembla {{gender:tous les gens|tous les hommes}} du lieu et fit un festin.
fr.B: Laban invita donc {{gender:tous les habitants|tous les hommes}} de l’endroit et donna un festin de noces.
fr.R: Alors Laban a invité à un repas de mariage {{gender:tous les gens|tous les hommes}} qui habitaient là.

sw.L: Labani akawakusanya pamoja wenyeji wote wa mahali hapo, akaandaa karamu.
sw.B: Basi Labani akawaalika watu wote wa mahali pale, akafanya karamu ya harusi.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Labani akawaalika watu wote walioishi pale kwenye karamu ya harusi.

decisions.choice: a feast (mishteh): a wedding banquet with wine
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "to drink". A wedding feast could last a week (verse 27; Judges 14:12, 17). Wine and darkness help Laban's plan.

decisions.choice: people (default), men (alternative)
decisions.reason: Anshei hammaqom is the population of the place in general, so the gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: {{gender:toda la gente que vivía|todos los hombres que vivían}}
decisions.reason: "La gente" takes a singular verb and "los hombres" a plural one, so the verb that agrees goes inside the span.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "wenyeji wote" (L), "watu wote" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Swahili "watu" and "wenyeji" already include women and men; "wanaume" would mean males only and change the sense, so Swahili has nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־לֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אֵלָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the evening, and he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.

en.L: And in the evening he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.
en.B: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob, and Jacob slept with her.
en.R: But that night Laban took his daughter Leah to Jacob instead of Rachel, and Jacob slept with her.

es.L: Y al anochecer tomó a Lea su hija y se la llevó, y él se llegó a ella.
es.B: Pero al caer la noche, Labán tomó a su hija Lea y se la llevó a Jacob, y Jacob se acostó con ella.
es.R: Pero esa noche Labán le llevó a Jacob a su hija Lea en lugar de Raquel, y Jacob se acostó con ella.

fr.L: Et le soir, il prit Léa, sa fille, et la lui amena, et il alla vers elle.
fr.B: Mais le soir venu, Laban prit sa fille Léa et la conduisit à Jacob, et Jacob s’unit à elle.
fr.R: Mais ce soir-là, Laban a amené à Jacob sa fille Léa au lieu de Rachel, et Jacob a couché avec elle.

sw.L: Jioni ilipofika, alimchukua binti yake Lea, akamfikisha kwake, naye akaingia kwake.
sw.B: Lakini jioni ilipofika, Labani alimchukua binti yake Lea, akampeleka kwa Yakobo, naye Yakobo akalala naye.
sw.R: Lakini usiku ule Labani alimpeleka binti yake Lea kwa Yakobo badala ya Raheli, naye Yakobo akalala naye.

decisions.choice: in the evening: the bride brought veiled, in the dark
decisions.reason: A bride was veiled when she came to her husband (24:65). In the dark, after the feast, Jacob did not know which daughter he had been given.

decisions.choice: he took Leah: the deceiver deceived
decisions.reason: Jacob, who deceived his blind father in the dark of his eyes (27:18-24), is deceived in the dark of night. The narrator makes no comment; the pattern speaks for itself.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, since Laban and Jacob are both "he" in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: instead of Rachel
decisions.reason: Readable makes the deception explicit.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לָ֔הּ אֶת־זִלְפָּ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לְלֵאָ֥ה בִתּ֖וֹ שִׁפְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Laban to her Zilpah his slave woman, to Leah his daughter [as] a slave woman.

en.L: And Laban gave Zilpah his slave woman to his daughter Leah as her slave woman.
en.B: (Laban had given his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah, to be her servant.)
en.R: (Laban gave his servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah to be her servant.)

es.L: Y dio Labán a Zilpá, su esclava, a su hija Lea como esclava.
es.B: (Labán le había dado a su hija Lea su sierva Zilpá, para que fuera su sierva).
es.R: (Labán le dio a su hija Lea su sierva Zilpá para que la sirviera).

fr.L: Et Laban donna Zilpa, son esclave, à Léa, sa fille, comme esclave.
fr.B: (Laban avait donné sa servante Zilpa à sa fille Léa, pour qu’elle soit sa servante.)
fr.R: (Laban a donné sa servante Zilpa à sa fille Léa, pour qu’elle la serve.)

sw.L: Naye Labani akampa binti yake Lea mjakazi wake Zilpa, awe mjakazi wake.
sw.B: (Labani alikuwa amempa binti yake Lea mtumishi wake wa kike Zilpa, awe mtumishi wake.)
sw.R: (Labani alimpa binti yake Lea mtumishi wake Zilpa, ili amtumikie.)

decisions.choice: Zilpah ... as a slave woman (shifchah): part of the bride's dowry
decisions.reason: A father might give his daughter a female slave at her marriage, as Rebekah went with her nurse and her young women (24:59, 61). The slave belonged to the wife, and later bore children for her (30:9-10).

decisions.choice: in parentheses
decisions.reason: The verse is an aside that interrupts the story of the wedding night; Balanced and Readable mark it as such.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m1) keeps that she was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: "mjakazi" (L); "mtumishi wa kike", "mtumishi" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Mjakazi" is the Swahili word for a female slave, the Literal counterpart of "mtumwa"; Balanced and Readable say "servant" as the English does.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּה־הִ֖וא לֵאָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־לָבָ֗ן מַה־זֹּאת֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לִּ֔י הֲלֹ֤א בְרָחֵל֙ עָבַ֣דְתִּי עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה רִמִּיתָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the morning, and look, she [was] Leah. And he said to Laban, what [is] this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel I served with you? And why have you deceived me?

en.L: And in the morning, look, it was Leah! And he said to Laban, "What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served with you? Why then have you deceived me?"
en.B: In the light of morning Jacob saw that it was Leah. "What have you done to me?" he said to Laban. "It was Rachel I worked for! Why have you tricked me?"
en.R: In the morning Jacob saw that it was Leah! He said to Laban, "What have you done to me? I worked for you to marry Rachel! Why did you trick me?"

es.L: Y por la mañana, he aquí, ¡era Lea! Y dijo a Labán: «¿Qué es esto que me has hecho? ¿No fue por Raquel que te serví? ¿Por qué, pues, me has engañado?».
es.B: A la luz de la mañana, Jacob vio que era Lea. «¿Qué me has hecho?», le dijo a Labán. «¡Yo trabajé por Raquel! ¿Por qué me has engañado?».
es.R: Por la mañana, ¡Jacob vio que era Lea! Le dijo a Labán: «¿Qué me has hecho? ¡Yo trabajé para ti para casarme con Raquel! ¿Por qué me engañaste?».

fr.L: Et au matin, voici, c’était Léa ! Et il dit à Laban : « Qu’est-ce que tu m’as fait là ? N’est-ce pas pour Rachel que j’ai servi chez toi ? Pourquoi donc m’as-tu trompé ? »
fr.B: À la lumière du matin, Jacob vit que c’était Léa. « Que m’as-tu fait ? dit-il à Laban. C’est pour Rachel que j’ai travaillé ! Pourquoi m’as-tu dupé ? »
fr.R: Le matin, Jacob a vu que c’était Léa ! Il a dit à Laban : « Qu’est-ce que tu m’as fait ? J’ai travaillé pour toi pour épouser Rachel ! Pourquoi est-ce que tu m’as trompé ? »

sw.L: Ikawa asubuhi, na tazama, alikuwa Lea! Akamwambia Labani, "Ni nini hiki ulichonitendea? Je, si kwa ajili ya Raheli nilikutumikia? Basi kwa nini umenidanganya?"
sw.B: Asubuhi kulipokucha Yakobo akaona kwamba ni Lea. "Umenitendea nini?" akamwambia Labani. "Nilifanya kazi kwa ajili ya Raheli! Kwa nini umenihadaa?"
sw.R: Asubuhi Yakobo akaona kwamba ni Lea! Akamwambia Labani, "Umenifanyia nini? Nilikufanyia kazi ili nimwoe Raheli! Kwa nini ulinidanganya?"

decisions.choice: and look, it was Leah!: the discovery seen through Jacob's eyes
decisions.reason: Hinneh lets the reader share Jacob's shock at daylight.

decisions.choice: deceived me (rimmitani): the same root as "deceit" in 27:35
decisions.reason: Isaac said Jacob came "with deceit" (mirmah) to take Esau's blessing. Now Jacob accuses Laban of the very thing, in a word from the same root.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן לֹא־יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן בִּמְקוֹמֵ֑נוּ לָתֵ֥ת הַצְּעִירָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַבְּכִירָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Laban, not it is done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.

en.L: And Laban said, "It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
en.B: "It is not our custom here," Laban replied, "to give the younger daughter in marriage before the firstborn.
en.R: Laban answered, "Here in our country we do not let the younger daughter marry before the older one.

decisions.choice: the younger before the firstborn: Jacob's own deed turned back on him
decisions.reason: Laban uses the word "firstborn" (bekhirah), the root of the birthright Jacob took from his older brother (25:31-34). Jacob put the younger before the firstborn at home; in Haran it is not done.

decisions.choice: it is not done so in our place: an appeal to local custom
decisions.reason: Laban appeals to custom, but he had agreed to Jacob's terms without mentioning it (verses 18-19).

source.text: מַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וְנִתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ גַּם־אֶת־זֹ֗את בַּעֲבֹדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמָּדִ֔י ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע־שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Complete [the] week of this one, and we will give to you also this one, for [the] service that you will serve with me yet seven years other.

en.L: Complete the week of this one, and we will give you the other also, for the service that you will serve with me for another seven years."
en.B: Finish out this one's wedding week, and then we will give you the other one too, in return for another seven years of work for me."
en.R: Spend this week celebrating your marriage to Leah. Then we will give you Rachel too. But you must work for me seven more years."

decisions.choice: complete the week of this one: the week of wedding celebrations
decisions.reason: A wedding feast lasted seven days (Judges 14:12). Jacob must keep Leah's week as her husband before he is given Rachel.

decisions.choice: another seven years: Rachel given at once, the work paid afterward
decisions.reason: Rachel is given after the week (verse 28); the second seven years of work follow (verse 30).

decisions.choice: Leah ... Rachel
decisions.reason: Readable names the two sisters for clarity.

source.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יַעֲקֹב֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיְמַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וַיִּתֶּן־ל֛וֹ אֶת־רָחֵ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And did Jacob so and completed [the] week of this one, and he gave to him Rachel his daughter to him as a wife.

en.L: And Jacob did so, and completed her week; and he gave him Rachel his daughter as wife.
en.B: Jacob agreed, and when Leah's week was over, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
en.R: Jacob agreed. When the week was over, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife too.

decisions.choice: Rachel as wife: two sisters married to one man
decisions.reason: The later Law forbade a man to marry his wife's sister while she lived, as a rival to her (Leviticus 18:18). The rivalry between the sisters fills the chapters that follow (30:1-24).

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ אֶת־בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לָ֖הּ לְשִׁפְחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Laban to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his slave woman, to her as a slave woman.

en.L: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his slave woman, to be her slave woman.
en.B: (Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel, to be her servant.)
en.R: (Laban gave his servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.)

decisions.choice: Bilhah as a slave woman: Rachel's dowry
decisions.reason: As with Zilpah and Leah (verse 24). Bilhah will later bear sons for Rachel (30:3-8) and be the mother of Dan and Naphtali.

decisions.choice: in parentheses
decisions.reason: As in verse 24, the verse is an aside.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); the meaning decision (m1) keeps that she was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ גַּ֣ם אֶל־רָחֵ֔ל וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב גַּֽם־אֶת־רָחֵ֖ל מִלֵּאָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמּ֔וֹ ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע־שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah; and he served with him yet seven years other.

en.L: And he went in to Rachel also, and he loved Rachel more than Leah; and he served with him another seven years.
en.B: Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he worked for Laban seven more years.
en.R: Jacob slept with Rachel too, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. He worked for Laban for seven more years.

decisions.choice: he loved Rachel more than Leah: the favoritism repeats
decisions.reason: Isaac loved Esau, and Rebekah loved Jacob (25:28). Now Jacob loves one wife more, and later one son more (37:3). Each time it brings pain to the family.

decisions.choice: Laban
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one Jacob worked for.

source.text: וַיַּ֤רְא יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־שְׂנוּאָ֣ה לֵאָ֔ה וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־רַחְמָ֑הּ וְרָחֵ֖ל עֲקָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw YHWH that [was] hated Leah, and he opened her womb; but Rachel [was] barren.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Leah was hated, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Leah was unloved, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let her conceive, while Rachel remained childless.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} saw that Jacob did not love Leah as he loved Rachel. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made it possible for Leah to have children. But Rachel could not have children.

decisions.choice: hated (senu'ah): loved less, not favored
decisions.reason: In matters of marriage, "hated" can mean the less favored of two wives (Deuteronomy 21:15-17). Verse 30 says Jacob loved Rachel "more", so Leah was loved less. To Leah it felt like being hated (verse 33).

decisions.choice: the LORD saw ... and opened her womb: God cares for the neglected
decisions.reason: As God saw Hagar in her misery (16:13), he sees Leah. Children are his gift: he opens the womb, and Rachel is barren, as Sarah and Rebekah had been (11:30; 25:21).

decisions.choice: unloved
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the word in this setting (m1); Literal keeps "hated".

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the LORD.

source.text: וַתַּ֤הַר לֵאָה֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ רְאוּבֵ֑ן כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֗ה כִּֽי־רָאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּעָנְיִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה יֶאֱהָבַ֥נִי אִישִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And conceived Leah and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, because has looked YHWH on my affliction; for now will love me my husband.

en.L: And Leah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has looked on my affliction; for now my husband will love me."
en.B: Leah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, saying, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has seen how I suffer. Surely now my husband will love me."
en.R: Leah became pregnant and had a son. She named him Reuben, which sounds like "He has seen my trouble." She said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has seen how unhappy I am. Now my husband will surely love me."

decisions.choice: Reuben: "look, a son", heard as "he has seen my affliction"
decisions.reason: The name sounds like re'u ben, "look, a son". Leah hears in it ra'ah be'onyi, "the LORD has seen my affliction". Hagar had named her well for the God who sees (16:11-14).

decisions.choice: my affliction ('oni): misery, humiliation
decisions.reason: The word is used of Hagar's misery (16:11) and of Israel's suffering in Egypt (Exodus 3:7).

decisions.choice: now my husband will love me: a hope not met
decisions.reason: Leah hopes a son will win Jacob's love. Her words with each son show how far the hope is from coming true (verses 33-34).

decisions.choice: which sounds like "He has seen my trouble"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

source.text: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי־שָׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־שְׂנוּאָ֣ה אָנֹ֔כִי וַיִּתֶּן־לִ֖י גַּם־אֶת־זֶ֑ה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And she conceived again and bore a son and said, because has heard YHWH that hated [am] I, and he has given me also this one; and she called his name Simeon.

en.L: And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, "Because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has heard that I am hated, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given me this one also." And she called his name Simeon.
en.B: She conceived again and had another son. "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has heard that I am unloved," she said, "and so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given me this son as well." So she named him Simeon.
en.R: Leah became pregnant again and had another son. She said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} heard that my husband does not love me, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave me this son too." She named him Simeon, which sounds like "he heard."

decisions.choice: Simeon: from shama, "he has heard"
decisions.reason: The name Shim'on sounds like the verb "to hear". God hears the cry of the unloved, as he heard Hagar (16:11; 21:17).

decisions.choice: which sounds like "he heard"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to the LORD.

source.text: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר עַתָּ֤ה הַפַּ֨עַם֙ יִלָּוֶ֤ה אִישִׁי֙ אֵלַ֔י כִּֽי־יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים עַל־כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא־שְׁמ֖וֹ לֵוִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she conceived again and bore a son and said, now this time will be joined my husband to me, for I have borne to him three sons; therefore he called his name Levi.

en.L: And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, "Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons." Therefore he called his name Levi.
en.B: Once more she conceived and had a son. "Now at last my husband will become attached to me," she said, "because I have given him three sons." That is why he was named Levi.
en.R: Leah became pregnant again and had another son. She said, "Now at last my husband will feel close to me, because I have given him three sons." So he was named Levi, which sounds like "joined."

decisions.choice: will be joined (yillaweh): Levi, "joined"
decisions.reason: The verb lavah means to be joined or attached; the name Levi sounds like it. Later the tribe of Levi was "joined" to Aaron to serve at the tabernacle (Numbers 18:2, 4).

decisions.choice: he called his name: the Hebrew has "he", not "she"
alternatives: she called his name (Samaritan Pentateuch, Septuagint)
decisions.reason: With the other sons Leah names the child (verses 32, 33, 35). Here the Hebrew says "he called", which may mean Jacob, or simply "one called", that is, "he was named". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read "she called". The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: he was named
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the verb as impersonal (m2).

decisions.choice: which sounds like "joined"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

source.text: וַתַּ֨הַר ע֜וֹד וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֗ן וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַפַּ֨עַם֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה עַל־כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד מִלֶּֽדֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And she conceived again and bore a son and said, this time I will praise YHWH; therefore she called his name Judah. And she stopped from bearing.

en.L: And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, "This time I will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." Therefore she called his name Judah. And she ceased bearing.
en.B: She conceived yet again and gave birth to a son. "Now I will give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," she said, and so she named him Judah. Then for a time she had no more children.
en.R: Leah became pregnant again and had another son. She said, "Now I will praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." So she named him Judah, which sounds like "praise." After that, Leah stopped having children for a while.

decisions.choice: Judah: from odeh, "I will praise"
decisions.reason: The name Yehudah sounds like the verb "praise, give thanks" (yadah). Jacob plays on it again in his blessing: "Judah, your brothers shall praise you" (49:8).

decisions.choice: this time I will praise the LORD: Leah's words change
decisions.reason: With her first three sons Leah spoke of her husband's love; now she speaks only of praising God. From Judah came David's royal line and, in the New Testament, Jesus (Matthew 1:2-16).

decisions.choice: she ceased bearing: for a time
decisions.reason: Leah later bears two more sons and a daughter (30:17-21). The pause sets up the next stage of the sisters' rivalry.

decisions.choice: which sounds like "praise"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the wordplay on the name (m1).

decisions.choice: for a time (B); for a while (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear the pause was not permanent (m3).
